page: The UpCloud GPU-20xCPU-256GB-3xL4 is a KVM-based virtual server built on the x86_64 CPU architecture. It is configured with 20 shared vCPUs and 256.0 GB of system memory, which establishes a high resource density of 12.8 GB of RAM per virtual core. This configuration does not include any local storage, meaning storage resources must be provisioned externally. One complimentary public IPv4 address is included with the deployment.

The primary performance driver of this server is its GPU subsystem, which features three NVIDIA L4 GPUs based on the Ada Lovelace architecture. Together, these three graphics processors provide a total of 72 GB of VRAM. The integration of multiple hardware accelerators makes this instance type highly capable of handling parallel processing tasks without relying solely on the host CPU.

Given the shared CPU allocation, this server is qualitatively optimized for workloads where the primary computational bottleneck is offloaded to the GPUs rather than requiring dedicated, continuous CPU cores. It is structurally suited for workloads such as machine learning inference, data science pipelines, parallel computing, and graphics rendering tasks that benefit from large GPU memory and high system RAM.
